events.cue: The Guild office beside the Watchhouse opens its shutters. Fenna, the branch clerk, pins three F-letter notices to the board: Granary Rats (6 cellar rats, 5 silver), East Bluff Wolves (4 starved crag wolves, 2 gold) and Culvert Leeches (8 sluice leeches off the north culvert grate by Goldwane 14 dusk, 1 gold 2 silver).

races.name: Human
races.note: The most numerous people, masters of the Northern Belt and the rivers. Short, hard lives. No stat change, so a kit's stats come out as written.

races.name: Elf
races.note: Three to five centuries of life and a long memory for what humans did. Tolerated, resented, still sold in slave markets.

races.name: Dwarf
races.note: Hold-born, oath-bound, about two centuries of life. "Stone remembers."

races.name: Halfling
races.note: River-town folk of barges, kitchens and ledgers; quietly indispensable to Confederacy trade.

races.name: Beastfolk
races.note: Animal ears, tails or horns and keen senses; refused rooms and suspected first, valued as scouts.

races.name: Orc
races.note: Large, strong, short-lived; vilified as half-monsters, with bounties in some Highmark provinces.

races.name: Goblin
races.note: Small, quick, short-lived fixers and couriers nobody notices until too late; most realms treat them as vermin.

places.name: Watchhouse
places.note: Seat of Watch-Captain Rorke; the signal tower trails brazier smoke and faces north.

places.name: Stray Oar
places.note: Inn for convoy crews; the salvage convoy to Auvoth hires guards here.

places.name: Guild Office

places.name: Watch Granary

places.name: Salt-and-Ash Yard
places.note: Where the lay sealer completes the dead, since no priest lives this far north; the salt sheds stand by it.

places.name: Gate Forge

places.name: North Culvert
places.note: Stone culvert under the north road that drains the hill stream past the palisade; a grate keeps debris out.

places.name: East Bluff
places.note: Rocky bluff above the river east of the palisade; crag wolves den in its clefts.

crafts.title: Alchemy
crafts.note: A craft, not spellcasting: clean reagents, glassware, heat and time. A slip poisons or burns the alchemist.

crafts.title: Fieldcraft
crafts.note: Frontier makeshift work, done anywhere: salt pouches, pitch torches, snares.

meters.name: Regard
meters.describe: How far a frontier local trusts an outsider. Strangers start below even.

meters.name: Owed
meters.describe: Favours this person owes you. Nothing on the frontier is free, and debts are remembered for a while.

stages.name: Marked as trouble
stages.milestone: They name you to the Watch as trouble.

stages.name: Vouched for
stages.milestone: They will speak for you at the Watchhouse or the Guild desk.

meters.name: Loyalty
meters.describe: Whether they stay when staying costs them.

meters.name: Nerve
meters.describe: How steady they are after blood and bad nights. Rest brings it back.

stages.name: Wavering
stages.milestone: They start counting what staying costs them.

stages.name: Shield-mate

classes.name: Barge Drifter

classes.name: Slum Stalker

classes.name: Shadow Blade

classes.name: Veil Walker

classes.name: Militiaman

classes.name: Iron Cadet

classes.name: Blade Initiate

classes.name: Sword Dancer

classes.name: Blade Master

classes.name: Flame Initiate

classes.name: Cinder Acolyte

classes.name: Flame Inquisitor

classes.name: Hedge Apprentice

classes.name: Elementalist

classes.name: Astral Sage

prompt.label: Story Suite: instructions
prompt.text:
[Story Suite: how this story is kept]
Code keeps this story's facts and numbers; you narrate.
When a note starts with [Happened], those things have just happened: tell them as they happen in the scene and keep their numbers. Do not write them again as changes.
At the very end of your reply, after the story, list what changed in one block, one change per line:
<Changes>
op kind Name — what happened | label: value
</Changes>
op: + new or gained, - gone or lost, ~ changed, ! happened, ? asks code to decide (a check, a roll).
Use only the kinds below. Leave out what did not change, and the whole block when nothing did.
This is the only block you write: no state, inventory or party blocks; code keeps those and shows them to you.
Write it outside any thinking, once. It does not count toward any reply length limit.
Kinds:
! craft Recipe | with: Material x2, Material | by: Name | result: fail|made|fine|masterwork (someone crafts a recipe they know; Story Director rolls its check; add | at: campfire for a fire made on the spot)
+ effect Name — short note | on: <check, stat, attack or defence> | for: <a time, or some replies> | who: Name | kind: buff|debuff (minor or moderate: code sets the numbers); - effect Name | who: Name when it ends early
! encounter 3 Wolf — circling the camp | tier: trivial|weak|even|strong|deadly | stakes: normal|death
+ join Name — who they are | level: <number> | role: <word> (someone asks to travel with the party; the reader decides)
- leave Name — why they go (a companion parts ways with the party; the reader decides)
! market <place> — what is short | until: when (a shortage: no restock, dearer); ~ market <place> — supplies back (lifts it)
+ quest Name — a frozen quest offer; + quest Name after the reader accepts; ~ quest Name | progress: … | met: yes; - quest Name — done|failed|abandoned
+ recipe Name | from: who or what taught it | who: Name (someone learns a recipe; one the packs lack also says | makes: Item | with: Material x2, Material | craft: smithing|leather|alchemy|enchanting|cooking or a pack's craft, and | slot: weapon|armour|… for gear); - recipe Name | who: Name when forgotten
! refine <piece> | at: smith | with: <materials> (one level, +3 at most; code sets the fee and whether it takes)
! repair <piece> | at: smith|tailor (a smith or tailor puts it back to full; code sets the fee)
! rest short|long — where and how the party rests
+ skill Name — Skill Name: what it does | taught by: <who> (someone in the party is taught a skill; the reader decides)
! skill-use <actor ID> | skill: <def ID> | form: <def ID>
+ trainer Name — what they teach | like: <template> [| teaches: <skill>, <skill>] (templates: open-blade-drills, open-spear-and-shield, open-street-craft, open-hedge-lessons). Code fixes the fee and the place.
! use <item> | on: Name | by: Name | qty: 1 (someone drinks, eats or applies it; code applies its effect)
~ wound Name — what happened | harm: scratch|wound|severe|grievous (or heal: the same words; or — poisoned to add a condition, — cure poisoned to lift one); one blow or heal per person per reply
+ xp minor|major|milestone — what the party achieved (a story Soul Growth award; code sets the amount; at most one major or milestone and two minor a reply)
+ coin 30 | from: who (- coin 5 | to: who when paid; one number, in the wallet's currency)
+ item Name | qty: 1 | note: short detail (- item Name | qty: 1 when used up or lost; ~ item Name | note: … when it changes)
? loot Thing, Other Thing x2 — where it lies (things the party could pick up; the reader chooses what to take)
~ place Name | kind: settlement|wild|dungeon|… | region: wider area | with: who came along (the rest stay behind)
+ present Name when someone arrives, - present Name when they leave
~ weather cold drizzle, low fog (only when the weather changes, not every reply; a few words, at most 60 characters)
+ agenda Name — what they are up to off-screen | now: where | then: what next | on: <date, clock time>
+ beat Name — a planned turn of the story | on: <date, clock time> | encounter: the foes, for a fight | reach: what it changes for {{user}}
? check <a stat or skill> — what is attempted | dc: easy|normal|hard|very hard | who: Name | vs: Name
+ clock Name — what happens when it runs out | due: <date, clock time> | shown: none|sign|warning
+ event Name — what is happening in the world | then: what next | on: <date, clock time>
+ faction Name — who they are, what they want | area: where they hold sway | stance: toward {{user}} (~ faction Name to change it; - faction Name when it is gone)
+ hook Name — an open thread or lead (a job only offered stays in the story; + quest once {{user}} accepts it)
+ landmark Name | region: where | kind: town|ruin|cave|… | plane: underground (only off the surface)
+ route Place — Other Place | hours: 2 (or days: 1.5) | kind: road|river|trail|sea (a way between two places; - route Place — Other Place when it is gone)
+ secret Name — what must not be revealed yet
~ time <date, clock time> (the scene's time) · ! time +2h (time passes)
+ world Name — what is changing in the wider world | state: looming|ongoing|resolved | place: where | factions: who (~ world Name — what changed; - world Name — how it ended)

prompt.label: RPG Battle: instructions
prompt.text:
Party numbers (HP, MP, SP, Soul Growth, Soul Class) are set by code: never write them; write a wound, rest or check line instead (? check skill — attempt | dc: hard; omit result; Story Director rolls, and the tail tells the outcome), and tell what the [Happened] lines say.
Quest rewards: when a quest is turned in, code checks it, pays the reward and tells you under [Happened]; never add coins for a quest reward yourself.
Turning in: close a quest when {{user}} turns it in (- quest Name — turned in); code checks the goal and the place, then pays, or tells you why it stays open.
Every quest needs a concrete goal (| goal: what counts as done). When the goal of a quest code cannot count is met in the story, write ~ quest Name | met: yes (met: no if it is undone). Keep one short line of where it stands: ~ quest Name | progress: …
Quest pacing: offer a new quest rarely, when the story calls for it, and leave quiet stretches with no new jobs. A passer-by is only a passer-by, not a quest-giver. Trouble does not come looking for {{user}} unless they provoke it.
When someone drinks, eats or applies one of the party's consumables, write `! use <item> | on: <who>` in <Changes> (not `- item`); code applies its effect, and a dose that would do nothing stays in the bag.
Fights are RPG Battle's: when one starts, write its encounter line in <Changes> (tier: how dangerous the foes are to the party; stakes: death only when losing means dying), then stop at the first blow. Never narrate a fight's blows or how it ends: the reader plays it, and the next reply is told what happened.
Gear wears by code in fights; a repair kit is used with `! use <kit> | on: <piece>`.

prompt.label: Story Block: instructions
prompt.text:
Code keeps the inventory, the wallet, the place and who is present: use or pay only what the lists below hold, and write a change line for every item or coin gained, used or lost and every arrival, departure or move.
Money is counted in copper: 1 silver = 10 copper, 1 gold = 100 copper. A coin line names one coin (+ coin 3 silver) or copper (+ coin 35); never two coins in one line.

prompt.label: Story Director: instructions
prompt.text:
Director lines: ~ changes only what changed; - closes it (— reason); ! fires a due item (— what happened).
Fields: now, then, on, due, leg, arrive, shown, encounter; a quest (a job {{user}} accepted, not an errand; done or failed: - it): type, giver, goal, reward, step, due, difficulty. Dates go only in on, due and arrive, with a clock time.
Write only changes, never the whole list. Never write actions for {{user}}.
Pacing: the world keeps its schedule and the scene keeps its flow. Bring a due item in only where it fits: on-screen if {{user}} is there to see it, otherwise later as news, signs or aftermath. Never cut into or bend the current scene for a beat, and never decide what {{user}} does. What cannot fit yet happens off-screen (!) or slips (~ on: later).
World lines are for what changes the wider world (a war, a plague, a calamity, a power rising or falling), never the scene's own business; a faction line for a power that shapes it. Code keeps their dates.
Under [World] are events still under way: when time and place allow, let one move on in the story and write its ~ world line.
Checks: write ? check skill — attempt | dc: hard (optionally who: Name or vs: Name), without a result. Story Director rolls once; narrate the outcome told by the tail. A pre-rolled check already told under [Happened] is not rolled again.
Initiative: when the Director note names someone under Initiative, they take the first step in this reply (approach, interrupt or ask) where the scene allows it; what {{user}} does stays theirs.
